name: Card
summary: A surface that groups a title and related content as one unit.
description: A card gathers what belongs together, a title and its content, on a raised surface with its own edge, so a page of many things reads as a grid of units: a project in a list of projects, a plan in a pricing page, a setting group. It is a surface, not a control: a card that opens something holds a link or a button; a card is never itself clickable. Its surface level follows the Color foundation.

anatomy.description: Root: the surface, with its edge, padding and corners. Carries the surface level; has no role of its own.
Heading of the card, at the level the page gives it.
Text under the title (the reference rendering's content; a product puts its own content here).

properties.name: Surface
properties.description: Surface level of the Color foundation the card is raised to; it sets the fill and the edge.

options.description: On a level 1 panel, or a card that must read as raised above its neighbours.

properties.name: Title
properties.description: What the card is about, as a heading.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Content of the card, as text.

properties.name: Heading level
properties.description: Level of the title in the page's outline, 2 to 6; cards in a list share one level under the list's heading.

states.description: The only state: a card has no interaction of its own.

notes: Title and content stack with container.gap inside the padding; the card fills the width its grid or list gives it.
Cards in a grid share a surface level and a heading level.

name.text: A card has no accessible name and no role: it is a generic container. Its title is a heading, which names the unit for people navigating by heading, and its content follows in the reading order.

guidelines.text: The structure of a card is programmatic: its title is a heading at a level that fits the page's outline, and the content follows it in the reading order; the surface conveys the grouping visually, the heading conveys it to assistive technology.
The title describes what the card is about, so people scanning headings can find it.

Render a div with no role and a heading element (h2 to h6) for the title; do not add role="article", "region" or "group" to a plain card, and never make the whole card a link or a button: put the control inside it.

Title and content contrast 19.07:1 and 12.87:1 (light), 10.32:1 and 8.06:1 (dark) on the level 1 surface, 19.07:1 and 12.87:1 (light), 9.45:1 and 7.38:1 (dark) on level 2; the edge is decoration (1.37:1 and 1.09:1 on level 1).
Mark the title with the heading semantics so services can navigate by heading.

references.title: ARIA in HTML: div element (role generic)
ARIA in HTML: h1 to h6 elements (role heading, aria-level)
HTML: the h1 to h6 elements (heading level)
WCAG technique H42: h1 to h6 to identify headings

guidelines: The title names the unit as a noun phrase: Quantum Design System, Team plan, Notifications. Sentence case, no trailing punctuation.
Keep the content short; a card that needs a lot of text is a section, not a card.

props.title: Quantum Design System
props.description: Technology-agnostic component specifications, DTCG tokens and a vanilla CSS reference implementation.

props.title: Team plan
props.description: Up to 20 members, unlimited projects and priority support.

decisions.text: A card is a surface of the Color foundation: level 1 by default (fill global.bg.level.1.default, edge global.border.level.edge.level.1) or level 2; it never defines a color of its own. The title is primary text, the content secondary text.
The surface has 16 px of padding, 8 px between title and content, a 0.6 px edge and 8 px corners; the title is the 16 px semi-bold heading style, the content 14 px body.
A card is never clickable as a whole and has no role; actions and links live inside it. Media, footers and actions as parts are open questions.

changelog.note: Initial draft (decisions surface-levels, box, not-a-control). A plain container on a surface level with a heading title and a text description; no interaction state. Contrast, light / dark: title 19.07 / 10.32 on level 1 and 19.07 / 9.45 on level 2, content 12.87 / 8.06 and 12.87 / 7.38; edge measured only.
